sources.title: Exact repository KMP/substring question and boundary audit

claims.text: The source requests substring matching and explicitly allows KMP or brute force, without preserving API/null/Unicode/all-match details.
The exact candidate KMP implementation matches Java first-occurrence String.indexOf semantics on fixed edge cases and 5000 deterministic randomized ASCII cases under the stated contract.
The candidate explains the no-text-backtracking mechanism and lps fallback that give KMP O(n+m) time and O(m) extra space.
Independent review found no hard failures or uncovered source variants and exhaustively validated the exact KMP fence against a separate brute-force oracle on bounded strings.

findings: The preserved source asks for substring matching and explicitly accepts KMP or brute force, but leaves API/null/Unicode/all-match semantics unspecified.
The candidate makes a narrow first-match Java String contract explicit instead of claiming those details came from the source.
The lps construction and mismatch fallback are explained through the no-text-backtracking invariant, with O(n+m) time and O(m) extra space correctly scoped.
The exact Java fence independently matches a separate brute-force oracle exhaustively for all binary strings with text length <=7 and pattern length <=5, plus UTF-16 and null-contract cases.
The answer contrasts brute force without dismissing it, identifies UTF-16 char indexing as a Java boundary, and does not fabricate project experience.
